sections.heading: Voltage-loop bandwidth
sections.text: Set the outer voltage-loop crossover well below twice the line frequency — typically 10 to 20 Hz for 50/60 Hz mains. A higher voltage-loop bandwidth distorts the current reference by passing the 100/120 Hz bulk-capacitor ripple into the inner loop, ruining input THD.

sections.heading: Twice-line-frequency notch
sections.text: Adding a notch or low-pass filter on the voltage-loop error at 2×f_line lets the loop tolerate the unavoidable bus ripple without distorting the current reference. Sizing the notch is more effective than dropping the loop bandwidth aggressively low — the latter hurts transient recovery on load steps.

sections.heading: Current-loop bandwidth
sections.text: Place the inner current-loop crossover near fsw/10 so the line-current waveform tracks the rectified sine reference with negligible phase shift. A current loop slower than line frequency / 100 will cause leading or lagging current distortion that registers as poor power factor regardless of THD.

sections.heading: Inrush handling
sections.text: PFC inrush limiting is rarely solved by the current loop alone. Verify the soft-start ramps the current reference rather than the duty, and that the bulk-cap pre-charge path is sized to avoid hitting the current limit during startup. Loop tuning cannot save a missing pre-charge resistor.
